newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African fruit export deregulation gets underway.
newsitem.headline: S.African fruit export deregulation gets underway.

text.p: The deregulation of South Africa's tightly controlled citrus and deciduous fruit export industry has got underway despite protests by control boards, National Agricultural Marketing Council chairman Eckart Kassier said.
Briefing the parliamentary agriculture committee on Wednesday, Kassier said that this was one of the "ticklish" issues the newly appointed council had already dealt with.

The council was appointed on January 6 to oversee the implementation of the new Agricultural Marketing Act which aims to do away with the single-channel marketing of the past and allow greater competition and representation of producers.

Kassier said that despite the single marketing channel operated in both the deciduous and citrus fruit industries, the council had granted a number of export permits to individuals and organisations outside these channels.
The ceilings for citrus were still being negotiated with the Citrus Board.
The Deciduous Fruit Board could not be reached to detail the number of permits granted.

Kassier said the granting of permits followed application by a number of parties to both boards to allow them to export fruit. Both had refused to issue permits on the grounds that the single channel was still in operation until the end of 1997.
The producers, however, had the right to appeal against decisions by the boards and Kassier said that "quite a lot of them" had appealed to the council.
Under the single channel marketing system, producers can export to any part of the world except North America, Europe and the Middle East, where they need special permits from the control boards.
